title: Introduce stream-shelf TTL + lease-fencing reconciliation for disconnected generations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Long-running streaming generations that are interrupted by client disconnects or client-side timeouts currently leave partial fragments in the system that consume memory/KV cache and confuse downstream tooling calls. Existing eviction logic is either too aggressive (leading to user-visible loss) or too lenient (wasting capacity). This ticket designs and implements a 'stream shelf' abstraction: a quarantined, short-lived buffer for interrupted generations with a small, server-managed TTL and a lease-fencing reconciliation protocol to decide final disposition (rehydrate, handoff, or hard-drop). The goal is to reduce wasted KV/cache units by 40% for interrupted sessions while preserving a 10s rehydration window for well-behaved SDK reconnections.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a stream-shelf with configurable TTL and max size per account
Implement lease-fencing tokens for each generation and ensure only the current lease-holder can rehydrate the shelf
Provide a tombstone ledger entry when fragments are hard-dropped for auditability
Add metrics: shelf_size_bytes, shelf_fragment_count, shelf_rehydrate_success, shelf_hard_drop_count
New system passes chaos test where 95% of reconnections within TTL rehydrate successfully and post-rehydration latency < 50ms median
Add integration tests for SDK-led detach + reattach flow and server-led hard-drop after TTL expiration
technical_notes: Stream-shelf sits logically between the active KV cache and long-term garbage collector. It stores compacted fragments (prefix fingerprints + compressed deltas) keyed by generation_id.

Each generation gets a lease token: <generation_id, epoch, holder_id>. On reconnect the SDK must present the last-seen epoch. If epoch matches current lease, rehydrate path allowed; otherwise return 'stale-lease' and trigger resume fallback.

Lease-fencing reconciliation: controller periodically scans shelf entries and compares record epoch against active session registry. If no active holder and TTL exceeded, emit tombstone and queue for compaction/hard-drop.

Backpressure/accounting changes: while on-shelf, fragments are charged at a reduced KV-cache weight but still count against account shelf_quota. This prevents unbounded accumulation from noisy clients.

Compatibility: SDKs that pre-date detach token support will fall back to existing orphan-sweep logic; server will maintain a compatibility shim that allows simple reattach where possible but flags these cases for telemetry.
Data retention and auditing: tombstone ledger entry contains generation_id, last_holder, drop_reason, dropped_at. Ledger persisted to append-only store for 30 days for incident analysis.
Failure modes: if compaction fails, entries are retried with exponential backoff; a monitoring alert will fire at >5% compaction failure rate over 5m window.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy shelf feature to 10% of hosts with shelf_ttl default 30s and shelf_quota=10MB per account. Observe metrics for 48h.
Phase 2 (expanded): enable for 50% after adding tombstone telemetry and SDK small-change release. Conduct chaos reconnection tests.
Phase 3 (general): enable for all accounts with adaptive shelf_ttl tuning based on workload class and implement auto-throttle when shelf_quota near limit.
Rollback: config flag shelf_enabled=false disables writes and triggers immediate hard-drop of new shelf writes, while existing entries still follow TTL.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Ava Chen: Initial spike complete. Proof-of-concept serializes prefix deltas and stores them in a compressed bucket. Measured per-fragment storage reduction ~3.2x.
2026-02-23 - Diego Morales: Implemented lease token schema and basic rehydrate handler. Need to decide canonical epoch bump semantics when a client reconnects from a different device.
2026-02-25 - Priya Nair (SRE): Request adding an alert on shelf_hard_drop_count > 1% of inbound streams for 10m; otherwise risk silent mass-dropping during infra incidents.
2026-02-27 - Design review: Agreed to expose a 'client_detach_reason' enum in rehydrate response so SDKs can surface better UX (user-abort vs network-blip).
2026-03-01 - Diego Morales: Canary deployment started on 10% of hosts. Observability dashboards added. Early telemetry shows shelf_rehydrate_success=92% at 30s TTL on chat-heavy workloads.
Follow-ups: add e2e test for function-call tool invocations that occur after rehydrate; ensure tool idempotency contract holds when rehydration resumes partial tool calls.
